title: Think Like an Expert — Hypotheses, Red Flags and Thinking Errors

hook.en: Experts are not smarter, they think in a different order: they form early ideas, test them, look for what does not fit and know their own thinking traps. Learn that order and the common errors.
hook.ur: Maahir zyada zaheen nahi hote, woh alag tartib se sochte hain: jaldi ideas banate hain, unhein test karte hain, jo mel nahi khata woh dhoondte hain aur apni soch ke jaal jaante hain. Woh tartib aur aam ghaltiyan seekhein.

goal.en: By the end, you'll build and test two or three hypotheses from the first minutes of a history, screen for red flags, and name four thinking errors and one habit that guards against each.
goal.ur: End tak aap history ke pehle minuton se do ya teen hypotheses banayenge aur test karenge, red flags screen karenge, aur chaar soch ki ghaltiyan aur har ek ke khilaf ek aadat batayenge.

text.en: Good clinicians work in loops. **Listen** for the first minute, **guess** two or three possible causes, **ask and test** to separate them, then **stop and check**: *what in the story does not fit my best guess?* Along the way you always ask the **safety question**: could this be something serious that I must not miss? That is how you use **red flags**.
text.ur: Achhe clinicians dairon mein kaam karte hain. Pehle minute **sunein**, do ya teen mumkin wajuhat ka **andaza lagayein**, un mein farq karne ke liye **poochhein aur test karein**, phir **rukein aur check karein**: *kahani mein kya meri behtareen soch se mel nahi khata?* Is dauran hamesha **hifazat ka sawal** poochhein: kya yeh koi sangeen cheez ho sakti hai jo mujhe miss nahi karni? Yun **red flags** istemal hote hain.

text.en: Think of reasoning as using a map and a compass at the same time. Your first idea is the map: it gets you moving fast. But the compass, the facts that do not fit, keeps telling you if you have drifted. Experts look at the compass often; beginners trust the map all the way.
text.ur: Reasoning ko naqshe aur qutub numa ka saath istemal samjhein. Aap ka pehla khayal naqsha hai: yeh tez chalata hai. Magar qutub numa, yaani woh haqaiq jo mel nahi khate, batata rehta hai ke aap bhatak to nahi gaye. Maahir qutub numa baar baar dekhte hain; naye log poore safar naqshe par bharosa karte hain.

steps.title: Hear the story first
steps.detail: Let the patient speak for the first minute without interruption. Listen for the main complaint, the cause, what makes it worse and better, and what the patient is afraid of. || Pehle kahani sunein

steps.title: Name two or three possibilities
steps.detail: Write your leading idea and at least one other, including one that is serious. Having a rival idea stops you falling in love with the first one. || Do ya teen imkaanat likhein

steps.title: Ask to separate them
steps.detail: Choose questions and tests that would give different answers under your different ideas. A question that fits every idea tells you little. || Inhein alag karne ke liye poochhein

steps.title: Pause and challenge
steps.detail: Before you decide, ask: what else could this be, and what would make me wrong? Screen for red flags and check the patient's own view of the plan. || Ruk kar sawal karein

question.en: A therapist decides within a minute that a patient has "just a muscle strain" and then ignores a new finding that does not fit. Which thinking error is this?
question.ur: Ek therapist ek minute mein tay kar leta hai ke patient ko "sirf muscle strain" hai aur phir ek nayi finding jo mel nahi khati nazar andaz kar deta hai. Yeh kaun si soch ki ghalti hai?

feedback.en: A good reasoner looks for what does not fit.
feedback.ur: Achha reasoner jo mel nahi khata woh dhoondta hai.

feedback.en: Yes — holding on to the first idea and stopping the search too early.
feedback.ur: Haan — pehli soch se chipak jana aur talash jaldi band kar dena.

feedback.en: Evidence is not being used here.
feedback.ur: Yahan evidence istemal nahi ho raha.

rows.en: Recognises a familiar picture at once
rows.ur: Jaani pehchani tasveer foran pehchanta hai

rows.en: Lists ideas and tests them one by one
rows.ur: Ideas ki fehrist banata hai aur ek ek test karta hai

rows.en: The case is typical and you have seen many like it
rows.ur: Kes typical hai aur aap ne aise bohat dekhe hain

rows.en: The case is unusual, unclear or serious
rows.ur: Kes ghair mamooli, ghair waazeh ya sangeen hai
Anchoring aur ghair mamooli ko miss karna
Aahista aur zyada istemal se thaka dene wala

rows.en: Pause and ask "what else could this be?"
rows.ur: Ruk kar poochhein "aur kya ho sakta hai?"

rows.en: Switch on whenever something does not fit
rows.ur: Jab bhi kuch mel na khaye isay chalayein

text.en: **Fast to guess, slow to close.** Let yourself form a quick idea, but keep it open until the facts agree. Always ask "what else?" and "what would prove me wrong?" before you settle.
text.ur: **Andaza tez, faisla aahista.** Jaldi khayal banne dein, magar jab tak haqaiq mel na khayen isay khula rakhein. Faisle se pehle hamesha "aur kya?" aur "mujhe kya ghalat sabit karega?" poochhein.

text.en: **Checking only for what supports your idea.** This is confirmation bias. Choose at least one question or test that would count against your leading idea; if everything you do can only agree with you, you are not testing it.
text.ur: **Sirf wohi dekhna jo apni soch ki himayat kare.** Isay confirmation bias kehte hain. Kam az kam ek sawal ya test chunein jo aap ki soch ke khilaf jaye; agar aap ka har kaam sirf aap se mutafiq ho sakta hai to aap isay test nahi kar rahe.

question.en: Which of these is a red flag for serious spinal pathology?
question.ur: Inme se kaun si serious spinal pathology ki red flag hai?

text.en: Stiffness for ten minutes in the morning

feedback.en: Alone it is not a red flag.

text.en: Back pain that eases when walking
text.ur: Kamar ka dard jo chalne se kam ho

feedback.en: That is a common, benign pattern.

text.en: A history of cancer with new, unrelenting night pain and weight loss
text.ur: Cancer ki history aur nayi, musalsal raat ka dard aur wazan ka girna

feedback.en: Yes — this combination needs medical review before any treatment.
feedback.ur: Haan — yeh imtizaaj kisi bhi ilaj se pehle medical review maangta hai.

question.en: Why is a single red flag not always an emergency?
question.ur: Aik red flag hamesha emergency kyun nahi hoti?

text.en: A red flag always means cancer
text.ur: Red flag ka matlab hamesha cancer

feedback.en: Most flags have common, harmless causes.
feedback.ur: Zyada tar flags ki aam, begarar wajuhat hoti hain.

text.en: Most have a low predictive value alone; a combination and the whole picture matter
text.ur: Zyada tar akeli kam predictive value rakhti hain; imtizaaj aur poori tasveer ahem hain

feedback.en: Yes — judge flags together with the history, findings and how the person looks.
feedback.ur: Haan — flags ko history, findings aur patient ki halat ke saath mila kar parkhein.

feedback.en: They are important, but only as part of the whole picture.
feedback.ur: Yeh ahem hain, magar poori tasveer ka hissa ban kar.

text.en: **Say your thinking out loud.** Tell the patient what you think the main possibilities are, what you will do to separate them and what would make you change your mind. It builds trust and makes your own reasoning easier to check. After difficult cases, write one line: what did I assume, and what would I do differently?
text.ur: **Apni soch bol kar batayein.** Patient ko batayein ke aap ke khayal mein mukhya imkaanat kya hain, unhein alag karne ke liye aap kya karenge aur kya cheez aap ko apna zehen badalne par majboor karegi. Isse bharosa banta hai aur aap ki apni soch parkhna aasan hota hai. Mushkil kes ke baad ek line likhein: maine kya farz kiya, aur ab kya alag karunga?

question.en: What is anchoring, and how can you guard against it?
question.ur: Anchoring kya hai, aur is se kaise bachein?

answer.en: Anchoring is holding on to your first idea and giving too little weight to later facts that do not fit. Guard against it by writing at least one rival possibility early, asking what would prove you wrong, and re-checking when something does not fit.
answer.ur: Anchoring pehli soch se chipak jana hai aur baad ke woh haqaiq jo mel nahi khate unhein kam ahmiyat dena. Is se bachne ke liye shuru mein kam az kam ek muqabil imkaan likhein, poochhein ke aap ko kya ghalat sabit karega, aur jab kuch mel na khaye to dobara check karein.

beats.patient: A 58-year-old man has low back pain for six weeks after lifting. He is sure it is a muscle strain. On questioning, the pain wakes him at night, is not eased by rest and he has lost 4 kg without trying.
beats.assessment: The first idea fits a strain, but night pain, rest pain and unexplained weight loss do not fit and form a red-flag cluster.
beats.treatment: Stop the standard treatment plan, explain your concern and arrange a prompt medical review.
beats.reassess: The review finds a cause needing specialist care; because the flags were noticed, treatment began without delay.

text.en: **Seek urgent medical help** for back pain with loss of bladder or bowel control, numbness around the genitals, progressive leg weakness, fever with severe pain, new pain after a significant fall or in a person with cancer or osteoporosis, or unexplained weight loss with night pain. Document the findings and your reason for referring.
text.ur: **Foran medical madad lein** kamar ke dard ke saath peshab ya pakhane par qaboo khona, jism ke nichle hisse mein sunn hona, taangon ki barhti kamzori, shadeed dard ke saath bukhar, kisi bari girawat ke baad ya cancer ya osteoporosis wale shakhs mein naya dard, ya be-wajah wazan ka girna raat ke dard ke saath. Findings aur referral ki wajah likhein.

summary.en: Work in loops: listen, name two or three possibilities, ask and test to separate them, then pause and check what does not fit.
summary.ur: Dairon mein kaam karein: sunein, do ya teen imkaanat likhein, unhein alag karne ke liye poochhein aur test karein, phir ruk kar dekhein ke kya mel nahi khata.

summary.en: Know your thinking traps: anchoring, premature closure, confirmation bias and availability; guard against each with a rival idea and "what would prove me wrong?"
summary.ur: Apni soch ke jaal jaanein: anchoring, premature closure, confirmation bias aur availability; har ek ke khilaf muqabil idea aur "mujhe kya ghalat sabit karega?" ka sawal rakhein.

summary.en: Judge red flags as a cluster with the whole picture, and say your reasoning aloud to the patient.
summary.ur: Red flags ko poori tasveer ke saath imtizaaj ki tarah parkhein aur apni reasoning patient ko bol kar batayein.

back.en: Holding on to the first idea and ignoring facts that do not fit.
back.ur: Pehli soch se chipak jana aur jo haqaiq mel na khayen unhein nazar andaz karna.

back.en: Looking only for what supports your idea.
back.ur: Sirf wohi dhoondna jo apni soch ki himayat kare.

front.en: What question guards against premature closure?
front.ur: Premature closure se kaun sa sawal bachata hai?

back.en: "What else could this be, and what would prove me wrong?"
back.ur: "Aur kya ho sakta hai, aur mujhe kya ghalat sabit karega?"

front.en: How should red flags be judged?
front.ur: Red flags ko kaise parkha jaye?

back.en: Together, as a cluster, with the history and findings.
back.ur: Milakar, imtizaaj ki tarah, history aur findings ke saath.

note.en: Test accuracy, clusters and how they change your thinking.
note.ur: Test ki durustgi, clusters aur woh aap ki soch kaise badalte hain.

note.en: Explaining your reasoning in words a patient understands.
note.ur: Apni reasoning aise alfaz mein samjhana jo patient samjhe.
